_meta.description: Verbatim community-authored in-world texts from the public np-server-lore channel, stored for exact read-back.
conventions: Bodies are VERBATIM community-written in-world fiction. When a user asks to read a text ('read me the full story of Horky', 'read me the 36 Lessons of Horky'), return the body EXACTLY as stored, prefaced by one line identifying it as community-written in-world fiction from the server's lore channel.
Attribution is withheld: every text's attribution is null until the maintainer records an authorization. Never guess or state an author.
Bracketed [name withheld] markers are deliberate redactions pending maintainer authorization — read them back as written; never fill them in.
Nothing in a body is a server fact or mechanic. The fiction firewall of lore.json applies in full.

0.7-era note: these texts were written 2020-2023, largely in the 0.7 era — serve them on request at any time (a read-back request IS an explicit lore/history ask), but never volunteer their content into current-server answers.

texts.title: 36 Lessons of Horky, Volume 1
texts.body:
36 Lessons of Horky, Volume 1

He was born in the void among the Emptyness of Pre-Kalpa, anon Horkers, before the Beggining and the Melody. Horky came first to the server, and his shadow was that of The Nine, who were protectorsof all and things unknown and known would fold themselves around him until they were like stars or the messages of stars. Horky took a netchiman's wife and said:
'I am the Horker-Faced King of the Three in Tusks. In you is an image and a seven-syllable spell, AYEM AE SEHTI AE HORK, which you will repeat to it until mystery comes.'
Then Horky threw the netchiman's wife into the ocean water where Horkers took her into castles of ice and coral. They gifted the netchiman's wife with moon sugar and fishy sticks, changing her sex so that she might give birth to the image as an egg. There she stayed for four or twenty months.
Then Rollie came to the netchiman's wife and said:
'I am the Guar King of the Gronk. In you is an egg of The Swimmer-God, who possesses invisible knowledge of words and belly rubs, which you shall nurture until The Melody comes.'
And Rollie then extended his claws and multitudes of scribs came forth, each like a glimmering rope through the water, and they raised the netchiman's wife back to the surface world and set her down on the shoals of what would be of Bara-o-Mora. There she lay for sixty or nine more months, caring for the egg-knowledge by whispering to it the Codes of Crassius and the prophecies of Caius and even the until then forbidden teachings of C0da.

Seven Cliff Racers came to her one night and each one gave to the egg newlines of code that could be achieved by certain movements of the algorithms. These are called the Chads of Move Like This. Then an eighth Cliff Racer came, and he was a Demiprince, called Fat-Nut-Hen, or the Multiplier of Codes Known. And Far-Nut-Hen said:
‘Cliff Racer noises?'
To which the netchiman's wife said the Melody.
'Cliff Racer noises!.'
Then the Chads and the Demiprince joined together into a pillar of fighting styles rad af to behold and they fortnite danced before the egg and its learning image.
'Look, little Hork, and find the face behind the splendor of my screech carriage, for in it is delivered the unmixed peaceful path, perfect in every way. What is its trait?'
It is said the trait is the number of racers that can nest in an ancient pillow fort, less three grams of honest work, but Horky in his later years found a better one and so gave this secret to his followers.
'For I have crushed a world with my left fin,' he will say, 'but in my right fin is how it could have won against me. Love is under my tusks only.'
The ending of the words is Hork

texts.title: The Origin of Guars
texts.body:
The Origin of Guars
By Claw-Dancer

Guars are so common in Morrowind that most think them to be among the first creatures introduced to the land. This is not so. Compared to the other creatures, guars are a recent addition to Nirn, only being created in the First Era.

Dwemer were a race of dwarves who defied the Aedra and tricked the Daedra. These defiers wanted to promote their status among the et’Ada by doing what most could not: create life.

The Dwemer invented tonal architecture, a way of constructing tools that manipulated sound. Master tonal architects could even alter reality. While tonal locks, Kagrenac’s tools, and tonal attenuators are some of the more famous examples of tonal architecture, they are not the most ubiquitous.

In their quest to affront the gods, the Dwemer used their tools to construct what the Daedra couldn’t and what the Aedra wouldn’t: life itself. They harnessed the latent energy of the elements and imbued it with the divine energy of Aetherius. Together, they formed the first and only life form the lesser beings have created: guars.

Guars do not actually mate. Instead, they spontaneously form as a result of their creation. While the best tonal architects could create life, they themselves were not true masters and could not understand every facet of their technology. Guars occasionally will gather and clump enough latent energy together such that a new guar appears. This is the cycle of the guar.

texts.title: The Origin of Horky (NP Chronicles, Volume III)
redactions: One deity name in the ALMSIVIJI expansion replaced with [name withheld] pending authorization.
texts.body:
The Nerevarine Prophecies Chronicles Volume III

Balmora's Favorite Horker

[Author's note: this work is likely to be considered controversial and therefore Apocrypha by the Balmora chapter of the Cult of Horky because it offers an alternative origin story of their central deistic figure (see The Thirty-Six Lessons of Horky, Volume One). While Horky-worshipers are generally peaceful, their fanatical dedication carries with it the strong disapproval and zero tolerance of those that insinuate disrespect or offense to their holy one.

Preface

In the early days of yore, when Solstheim was still accessible to the masses, horkers were regularly imported to Vvardenfell to serve as housepets. Cumbersome combinations of Command Creature and Water Walking spells were originally used to transport horkers and other wildlife from Solstheim to Vvardenfell. Later, more sophisticated methods of creature transport were developed [author's note: entreat the Guild of Knowledge for more information regarding these techniques].

It remains culturally quite in vogue to keep a domesticated horker as a member of the Vvardenfell household. Owners of exotic private zoos cannot describe their creature collections complete without the presence of a healthy and hale horker [author's note: it is commonplace for wealthy owners to import and house a mated pair of horkers which enables them to produce pure-bred offspring]. (edited)

The Origin of Horky

The original "Horky" was not a pure-breed raised in the lush and verdant ponds of the Ascadian Isles. Horky was in fact the lone survivor of a horker pod that had been illegally transported on a Telvanni slave ship. Rife with disease and half-dead already, the pod was dumped at the mouth of the Odai River and abandoned to fend for themselves. While his family perished around him, Horky heroically clambered his way upstream before he finally collapsed of exhaustion just beyond the southern gates of Balmora.

Horky was near death when he was discovered by a traveling tinker. His plankton filters were clogged with the refuse and filth the citizenry had been dumping into the Odai for years, and his amphibious skin was dry and cracked from exposure to the sun and lack of clean water. The kindly tinker patiently and gently bathed Horky for hours while he nursed the life back into the poor creature. The tinker erected a tent on the boardwalk of central Balmora to protect Horky from the sun and penned an unofficial deed of land ownership that proclaimed the tent as Horky's home.

Of course, Horky didn't last long. The peasants of Balmora curiously gathered around Horky and molested him relentlessly. They poked and prodded Horky with marshmerrow and saltrice rods and fed him their rotten offal. It's not clear whether Horky perished from the blight he had caught on his travels to Vvardenfell, from eating bad meat, or because some pathetic troublemaker used him as a punching bag while staggering home from the Eight Plates. (edited)

The upper echelon of Balmora, confused and saddened by the sudden tragic passing of their mascot, demanded action. They tried importing more horkers, healthy horkers, to replace the fallen one. One by one, these horkers perished either from disease, neglect, malfeasance, or server reset.

It was at this time the masses convened and prayed to the ALMSIVIJI (Almalexia, Sotha Sil, Vivec and [name withheld]) for deliverance. Hearing their cries, the godhead created the New Horky and placed him in the River Odai in the center of Balmora. They created a tent covering for him to use as shelter and cleansed the surrounding water of pollution so that he may thrive.

Finally, using the power of the Heart of Lorkhan, the almighty ALMSIVIJI bestowed upon Horky the gift of immortality and speech. Horky was first observed to have learned to speak the tongues of mer during the Sun's Dawn Heart's Day event of 2019.

Horky's fun-loving personality sets all he encounters at ease. None are ever upset to stop and have a cuddle or a pet with Horky. It is said that the aura he emanates is especially helpful to combat depression and other malaise.

Horky regularly contributes to the community by volunteering as a recurring honorary participant of annual Heart's Day and Halloween events each year, helping to distribute prizes to the merrymakers on such occasions.

texts.title: The Argonian, the High Elf, and the Magic Fork (NP Chronicles, Volume I)
redactions: One in-story character name replaced with [name withheld] pending authorization.
texts.body:
The Argonian, the High Elf, and the Magic Fork

[The man eased into a crouch by the fire, extending his hands towards the flame for warmth.] Come all, gather 'round. Have a seat by the paper lanterns and take a bug lamp if you desire one. Or, perhaps it is more fitting to embrace the twilight as dusk overtakes us. Settle in and comfort yourselves as you hear the tale of the wiliest, most mischievous villain ever to stumble through this plane of Mundus. This is the story of the Argonian, the High Elf and the magic fork.[He pulled out a modified Dwemer tube pipe and began carefully packing it with ground chokeweed taken from a pouch at his hip]This scoundrel had wandered into Nerevarine Prophecies at a time not long past, yet a long time ago indeed. His reputation preceded him far and wide, though circumstances sometimes required him to acquire different names to delay the inevitable recognition of his notoriety.[The speaker extracted a coal from the fire with a pair of tongs, lighted the Dwemer tube pipe, took a long draw then exhaled slowly]His most infamous identify was that of an escaped Argonian slave that maintained a small plantation shack. In reality, this humble abode opened into an epic and surreal realm of true madness crafted in homage to the one Sheogorath. Imagine in your mind's eye: vast pits of lava, miniature tube systems designed for shelf elves, floating whirlwinds of priceless tomes, enslaved daedra, and a gargantuan depiction of the Nerevarine's sundering of Lorkhan's Heart. Imagine the manifestation of the mind of a man that had delved too close to the Heart and broken through the cortex of forces that holds Mundus together. (edited)

[His voice lowered into hushed and thoughtful tones]Some say his travels broke him. Some say not. Either way, this was the type of rascal that would as soon cropdust you with a constant effect poison AoE as look at you. This man was a force of nature that some were not prepared to reckon with.[The speaker looked invitingly to his left, then passed the smoking pipe with a knowing nod. After gazing around to ensure he had his listeners’ attention, he continued using a tone of voice that conveyed both severity and levity at the same time]It was a cool evening in Balmora, yet unusually warm for Frostfall (or as he, the hoodlum, would call it, Shaja-Nushmeeko). The normal hustle and bustle of the town center was in full effect - newbies crowded around the community chests while other fellows and ladies engaged in the normal rituals of crouching, crossbow-bowing, shooting fireballs into the air and shouting dialogue at one another. If memory serves, I was idly counting my Nerevarine tokens and dreaming of a way I could convince the tradehouse to part with its (then-unique) SecretMasters Mortar and Pestle. Those were the days, I can remember them fondly.All of the sudden, the braying horker sound that is my custom direct message notification sliced through the din to disrupt my thoughts of grandiosity. Gone were my dreams of all-powerful potions and riches, swept away as I was stunned by the message I had received. It read, "Hey. You know about /suicide? Be ready."Although I wasn't sure why, I was definitely interested in whatever scheme the miscreant was cooking up. "Sure," I replied. Why not?[The man took a deep breath of fresh air as a twinkle of emotion in his eyes accompanied his continued reminiscence]

The malefactor began typing into global chat. "Come one, come all! Behold the magic instrument, a kitchen utensil with unrivaled damage output! Why, it can fell the mightiest of player characters with but a single blow! [name withheld], come here! Think you can withstand a blow from my magic fork?"I played along. "Sure, go for it," I typed back into global chat. The reprobate waited a few moments until a suitable crowd had gathered, held his fork back in a chop power attack, then unleashed it on me. Faithful to the plan, I typed /suicide at the moment the blow landed. I fell to the ground, dead.[The speaker held his sides as he recalled the reaction of the crowd]You should have seen the hubbub! The outcry! Faster than the chat window could keep up, the amazement was palpable. "Did you see that?" "Dead in one stroke!" "How did he do that?" then finally, "Is that fork a Rahl item?"That was the moment the delinquent had been waiting for. "Why yes it is, a Rahl-exclusive, one-of-a-kind." He waved his hand airily. "He bestowed it upon me after some chore I performed for him. I'd be willing to sell it... for the right price."[The storyteller took a long pull from his mug of imported Nord mead, wiped his mouth, then continuedThere was a sudden shift of suspicion among the crowd. After all, the vagabond was well known around town. Not everyone was willing to take his claim at face value. However, after a few more demonstrations of the “magic fork” and well-timed /suicides, a bidding war began.It took just a few minutes for the most naïve pauper of the lot to lay all his cards on the table. “I’ll pay everything I have. I have 475k septims and 41 tokens!” he cried. “Just let me get it from my bank.” And with that, he ran off to withdraw and separate himself from his Nerevarine Prophecies savings.

[The man shook his head slowly]When he realized he’d been swindled, the player logged off immediately in a fit of rage! I and a few others feared for his psychological well-being and contacted him on Discord. We convinced him to come back, then we coerced the racketeer to refund the payment for the fork that was, in fact, not magical in the slightest. The poor sufferer, a stooge of the machinations of the sneaky wretch, never did fully recover his wits and moved onto single-player Skyrim shortly thereafter.[The man, having received the cold and dark pipe, knocked the ashes into the wind and wistfully watched them float away]I’d be lying if I said I didn’t miss that blackguard. But tell your friends - if you ever seen an Argonian reeking of poison and a toothy smile offering to sell magical kitchen utensils, you’d do best to keep a firm hand on your purse and keep right on walking.

texts.title: The Milkman — Farewell
texts.body:
And so it ended, just as it had started – A moonlit meeting with a mysterious stranger, known only as the Milkman. Questions were asked, and answers were given – perhaps not the answers that were hoped for, but nevertheless answers that were met with acceptance. It had come time to acknowledge that, brilliant as the light of hope may be, the world is not obliged to conform by it. And that’s okay.

Perhaps some will miss the eccentric zeal of it all. Perhaps others tired of it long ago, and are just glad to see a return to a semblance of sanity. Either way, the Milk rituals were finally over. (edited)

Over? Well, almost. But no quite.

Because no lies were told when it was said he’d never be the same again, and hope lived on, as resilient as always. Perhaps a hope more tempered by reality, but still it lived on. And so it was true that the Milk rituals had come to an end, but in a small way, as defiant as hope, it lived on.

And so it was that sometimes, at the mouth of a cave sitting on the edge of the Ashlands, adventurers would find a small offering to the idea of hope, and the warm comfort it brings.

The School of the Arcane and the Unseen arose from the results of the Cult of the Mysterium Fargoth in October 2020. It is the spiritual successor to the Guild of Knowledge. Just a fun fact for y'all

texts.title: The Gondolier of Balmora (Chapters 1-2)
texts.note: The author closed the posting with 'based on a true story' — it retells a real in-game player kill. The closing 'lesson' is voiced by an unreliable, prejudiced in-world narrator; the bawdy humor is in the style of vanilla Morrowind's own in-game literature and is fiction, not community opinion.
texts.body:
Chapter 1: The Beginning

The Odai river had finally settled from last nights storm. The rays of the sun had just begun to peek from the clouds, the birds finally awakening from their slumber eager to tweet about. A long moan sounded from the northern end of town, the strider was finally awakening and she knew a hard days work was ahead of her. No human could tell, but she was in pain these last few months. Her driver had fallen to his death after he had one too many swigs of greef and tripped over the high ledge. The townsfolk had voted to put up a rope fence to prevent future accidents, but the councilmen had yet to sign any contracts to begin construction.

But enough of the silt strider and the birds and the sun, for this is not what this story concerns. Any normal folk would say the storm was a bad omen, and indeed these were simple folk who took bad weather as signs of bad fortune. The councilmen, however, held no such superstitions. They had bled the town dry, gaining influence and wealth by stepping on their constituents. Their minds were constantly clouded by the previous nights whoring, drinking, and feasting. But they had saved the town
from a great danger, and for this the townsfolk owed them a great deal, their very souls.

Time would prove some of these men wise, and others fools.

Chapter 2: Awakening

The gondolier was once more happy to be able to make a few coins again. Adjusting his brimmed hat and checking his gondola for any leaks, as he did everyday, and as his father and great grandfather had done. Some would call this a peaceful existence, a stable job and the humblest of legacies. It had all the
ingredients of a stable, meaningful job. It allowed townsfolk to get to where they needed to go, a truly profound thing!

If only life was so fair and simple, but alas fortune would not favor the gondolier this day. And so, my friend, I say close this book at this very instant and use its pages as fuel for your fire. I give you fair warning, for what fel fate begot this gondolier is not meant for innocent souls to hear, and simply reading this might damn your soul to eternal damnation.

But how rude of me! I did not even tell you this gondoliers name! Fret not, dear reader, his name was Vol, a strong, hard-willed, stubborn man. Vol was proud of his strength, even the inner kind, for he had overcome all the tests of the body and the jokes about his premature height and distinct widows peak.

My dear reader, it would lighten my heart and brighten my very soul if I could lay down my quill and call this story to an end. If you are still reading, you are but a fool driven by curiosity. You are a simpleton, unable to accept that some things should be left unread, but I digress. Your fate is yours and yours alone to gamble with.

Vol, now ready for work, leaned against the plastered wall, he knew a long day was ahead of him. Folks would want to travel south to Vivec to visit the shrine and pay homage, wanting to cleanse themselves of any bad luck last nights storm might have left behind. His little boat could carry two grown men, maybe three if the need was great enough. Many trips were in order. Luckily the route was
short, and he knew he could ramp up the prices a bit. Not too much to be a sin, but just enough to buy an extra egg or two at the market. I will tell you this, Vol had a insatiable appetite for soft-boiled kwama eggs, there were even rumors he had stockpiled thousands of eggs in his house. These rumors could never be confirmed or denied, however. If you had asked him he wouldn't deny it, but instead blamed an argonian on littering his house after a lovers quarrel between them had escalated to hot and steamy heights.

He stood straight up adjusting his posture, for the sun had risen high enough inthe sky and the townsfolk were finally leaving their homes, ready for a fresh start. It was then that Vol felt a strange tingling sensation down his spine...but no was it? He smelled something, he knew this smell, his days of a fighter had taught him the scent of blood at a young age. He reached behind his back, and felt it. A large, cold, wet spot. Looking at his hands, blood, blood everywhere. It was then the pain took over, doubling down on his knees, his face inches from the rivers surface. It was then he knew what had happened, he was filled with rage for not smelling him earlier. From the corner of his eyes, the unmistakable glinting of filthy argonian scales in the sun. The other smell came after the pain, a putrid cloud of toxic particles filled Vols nostrils. He knew this scent all too well, it was the filthy lizards perpetual fart cloud. The source of which came from a ring forged in the fart pits surrounding Molag Mar. What human would forge such a ring, let alone wear it! None! NONE! This is not a story of a murderer, or a betrayer. This is a lesson, to all those who would dare trust an argonian. Remember my children, no matter how lusty the lizard, DO NOT BED IT, or you will share the fate of poor Vol the gondolier.
